newsitem.title: USA: Aetna posts sharp loss in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Aetna posts sharp loss in fourth quarter.

text.p: Aetna Wednesday reported a loss in the fourth quarter after taking major charges it announced previously to slash 4,400 jobs and restructure its health care and retirement services units.

Aetna lost $107.1 million, or 80 cents a share, in the quarter, as one-time items reduced operating income by $280 million after taxes. These include $301 million in severance and facilities, and other charges in Aetna U.S. Healthcare that wiped out a $21.0 million gain from a drop in the discontinued products reserves in Large Case Pensions.
A year ago, Aetna earned $175.7 million, or $1.53 a share.
However, full-year profits soared to $651.0 million, or $4.74 a share, thanks to $85.9 million of net realised capital gains and $445.9 million from discontinued property-casualty operations.
In 1995, Aetna earned $251.7 million, or $2.21 a share, including $29.5 million of capital gains and $222 million of net losses from the discontinued property-casualty operations.
Revenues jumped 33 percent to $4.49 billion in the fourth quarter from $3.37 billion in the 1995 period. They rose to $9.29 billion from $7.51 billion for the year.

"Aetna has reinvented itself as a new, leaner enterprise, composed of three complementary businesses linked in a common focus on growth and shareholder value," said Ronald Compton, chairman of the Hartford, Conn.-based company.
"Aetna U.S. Healthcare is rapidly combining the strengths of its two predecessors and is right on schedule in our mission to create the nation's premier health care company."
Including the unusual items, Aetna U.S. Healthcare reported a net operating loss of $214.1 million in the fourth quarter.
Total assets under management rose to $32.0 billion as of Dec. 31, a 20 percent increase, excluding a $2.0 billion transfer of assets from Large Case Pensions.

Aetna International, which sells life and health insurance as well as financial services products in emerging markets, saw fourth-quarter operating earnings rise to $27.1 million from $24.5 million a year ago. The improvement was driven by strong business growth in established markets, particularly Taiwan and Chile.

Large Case Pensions, which manages a variety of retirement and other savings products for defined benefit and defined contribution plan customers, reported fourth-quarter operating earnings of $51.3 million, up from $21.0 million a year ago. Fourth-quarter 1996 earnings include a $21.0 million after-tax benefit from a reduction in discontinued product reserves.
Aetna's stock fell $2.625 to $79.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
